More importantly, CARLA's own stock layout shows FIX_A is the wrong direction. The meshes are already in the CARLA-canonical place; it is the serialized references that are wrong.

carla_stock_layout.map_folder_contents_example: TownNN.umap + TownNN_BuiltData.uasset + TownNN_Opt.umap, and NO building StaticMeshes beside them
carla_stock_layout.conclusion: CARLA separates maps from building meshes. Town maps reference their buildings from /Game/Static/<Tag>/<MapName>/, NOT from the map's own folder.

ingolstadt_layout.pattern_match: EXACTLY matches the stock /Game/Static/Terrain/<MapName>/ pattern used by Town03..Town15
ingolstadt_layout.map_folder: /Game/Ingolstadt/Maps/Ingolstadt/ = Ingolstadt.umap + MAT_*.uasset + OpenDrive/ + TM/, and NO building meshes

decisive_evidence.conclusion: The 5711 building meshes are in the CARLA-canonical location. The tile-map serialized references are the defect: they point into the map folder, which diverges from the Town convention. FIX_A would move 72 MB of correct assets out of convention and duplicate them, making the map layout non-CARLA-like, to satisfy references that are themselves wrong.

corrected_diagnosis.authority_evidence: 9 stock CARLA town maps use Static/Terrain/<MapName>/; none place building meshes beside the .umap.

props_channel_is_not_the_cause.implication: props is EMPTY for this package, and Import.py builds props_dest only from prop['tag']/prop['name']. So the Static/Terrain/Ingolstadt path was NOT produced by the props channel as I hypothesised earlier; it comes from CARLA's own large-map/Terrain generation, which is the same mechanism stock towns use.
